name: Easing
summary: A move speeds up from rest and slows down before it stops, as a real mass does, instead of a constant speed.
how: Give a move of 200 to 400ms an ease-out curve when an element enters and an ease-in curve when it leaves.
Use cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) as the standard curve for a move inside the screen.
Put more frames at the two ends of a move than in the middle: 2 to 3 times the density.

origin.note: Animators draw more frames at the start and the end of a move; Thomas and Johnston name it slow in and slow out.

adoptions.via: Robert Penner publishes easing equations for Flash, and web motion takes them up.
CSS transitions define timing functions such as ease-in-out and cubic-bezier().

sources.title: Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston, The Illusion of Life: Disney Animation (1981)
Robert Penner, Programming Macromedia Flash MX (2002)
